summaries.label: Golden cross (20/50)
summaries.definition: The 20-bar average closed above the 50-bar average after being at or below it the bar before.
summaries.caveat: Moving averages lag by construction: by the time they cross, much of the move that caused the cross has already happened. A cross describes the recent past, not the future.

summaries.label: Death cross (20/50)
summaries.definition: The 20-bar average closed below the 50-bar average after being at or above it the bar before.
summaries.caveat: The dramatic name is marketing, not mathematics. It is the same lagging average comparison as the golden cross, pointed the other way.

summaries.label: RSI entered oversold
summaries.definition: RSI(14) closed below 30 after being at or above 30 the bar before.
summaries.caveat: 'Oversold' means recent losses dominated recent gains -- it does not mean 'due for a bounce'. In persistent declines RSI can stay below 30 for weeks.

summaries.label: RSI entered overbought
summaries.definition: RSI(14) closed above 70 after being at or below 70 the bar before.
summaries.caveat: 'Overbought' means recent gains dominated recent losses. Strong uptrends hold RSI above 70 for long stretches; this is not a sell signal.

summaries.label: MACD crossed above signal
summaries.definition: The MACD line closed above its signal line after being at or below it.
summaries.caveat: Built entirely from moving averages, so it confirms moves already underway and produces frequent false crossings in sideways markets.

summaries.label: MACD crossed below signal
summaries.definition: The MACD line closed below its signal line after being at or above it.
summaries.caveat: The mirror of the bullish cross, with the same lag and the same tendency to whipsaw when the price is drifting sideways.

summaries.label: Closed above upper Bollinger band
summaries.definition: The close finished above the 20-bar average plus two standard deviations, having been inside the band the bar before.
summaries.caveat: Statistically unusual is not wrong: prices ride the upper band through strong rallies. Treating a band touch as a reversal is a common and expensive mistake.

summaries.label: Closed below lower Bollinger band
summaries.definition: The close finished below the 20-bar average minus two standard deviations, having been inside the band the bar before.
summaries.caveat: An unusually large decline relative to recent volatility. It describes the size of the fall, not whether it is finished.

summaries.label: Unusually large single-bar move
summaries.definition: The bar's return exceeded 3 standard deviations of the trailing 252-bar return distribution (computed from prior bars only).
summaries.caveat: Large moves cluster: one outsized bar often sits inside a volatile stretch rather than ending one. The threshold uses only history available before the bar, so early data has no baseline and is skipped.

summaries.label: Recovered a 10%+ drawdown
summaries.definition: The close regained its prior running peak after having fallen at least 10% below it.
summaries.caveat: Recovery marks the round trip back to a previous high -- the money lost in between was real, and nothing about recovering one drawdown prevents the next.

method: Every event is detected using only bars at or before its own date: rolling statistics trail, baselines end one bar earlier, and a guard test mutates all future bars to prove past detections cannot change. Outcome tables then report what actually followed each event over 5, 20, and 60 later bars -- future bars are used only to describe history, never to decide that an event occurred. Events too close to the end of the data are excluded from a window and counted.
disclaimer: These are descriptions of past market behavior, not signals and not forecasts. A pattern that was followed by gains in this history carries no promise of repeating, and small samples -- which are flagged wherever they occur -- can look meaningful purely by chance.
